objectives.objective: Identify the owner, interpreter, and security consequence at a Python trust boundary.
objectives.learningEvidence: boundary map with assumptions and named sinks

objectives.objective: Trace a value from source through validation to a sink without treating generated code as trusted.
Write an AI coding requirement that includes constraints, assumptions, tests, and review checkpoints.
Explain why AI-generated output cannot independently authorize a grade, security decision, or release.
objectives.learningEvidence: human verification decision with residual-risk note

objectives.objective: Derive a Python allowlist from type, length, range, and feature grammar requirements.
Use parameterized data access for SQL values and allowlist any structural identifier choice.
objectives.learningEvidence: query control matrix and regression tests

objectives.objective: Prevent command injection by using a fixed executable, argument list, and explicit subprocess policy.
Reject eval and exec as input handling mechanisms and identify code-execution sinks.
Keep SQL values separate from SQL syntax when reviewing Python database code.
Select safe, data-shaped parsers and explain why pickle is unsafe for untrusted input.
Constrain YAML or JSON object shape before application use.
Distinguish a test fixture with a trusted integrity boundary from a deserialization path exposed to users.
Store uploads under generated names and enforce canonical containment beneath an authorized base.
Treat upload metadata and content as untrusted and apply size, type, and storage policy.
Apply scheme, hostname, IP, redirect, timeout, and egress controls to outbound requests.
objectives.learningEvidence: SSRF policy and URL test matrix

objectives.objective: Recognize when a remote URL or redirect is fixed configuration rather than user-controlled network authority.
Choose output encoding or safe rendering for the actual HTML, URL, header, or JSON context.
Explain when CSRF defenses are required and specify a server-verified token or origin policy.
Separate safe client errors from correlated, redacted operator diagnostics.
Identify a safe autoescaped template case without generalizing that safety to raw output or another context.
Distinguish authentication, authorization, ownership, and client presentation checks.
Deny BOLA/IDOR when an authenticated subject substitutes another valid object identifier.
Specify secure session rotation, expiry, revocation, and cookie transport controls.
Apply default deny and uniform failure behavior when no authorization rule grants an action.
Minimize secret collection and prevent secrets from entering prompts, source, responses, or logs.
Use an approved secret provider and design safe redaction across errors, traces, and support exports.
Triage dependency findings using ownership, reachability, affected path, and upgrade evidence.
Review package and build provenance without treating a scanner result as proof of safety.
Turn a feature requirement into a bounded Vibe Coding prompt with security acceptance criteria.
Review generated Python using vulnerable, secure, and false-positive examples for a selected category.
Use tests to challenge generated code, request an AI repair, and independently re-verify the repair.
objectives.learningEvidence: test result, repair diff, and human re-verification

objectives.objective: Decide whether a secure Python application meets requirements while recording residual risk and evidence gaps.
objectives.learningEvidence: capstone review decision; no executable deployment implied
